besu.name: Besu
besu.summary: Start with failed-frame reporting, precompile output and inclusion, and range-filter consistency. Individual replay also needs a scope decision.

erigon.name: Erigon
erigon.summary: The development build agrees on tree lookup, default filter composition, MCOPY, historical system state including trace_callMany, the genesis reward, omitted trace_filter bounds (#24341), reverted-CREATE results and failure labels (#24355, #24356) and failed-CREATE filter matching, several of which still differ in 3.7.0. Since #24330 and #24343 its trace_call prices gas like eth_call, keeps the block GASLIMIT and returns the eth_simulateV1 codes. It validates signed transactions at the selected state (#24329) rejecting each for its own violation (with -32000; the error-group codes are recommended); a filter bound past the head still returns [] (#24357 is open) and vmTrace still keeps halted-operation details (#24344 is open).

nethermind.name: Nethermind
nethermind.summary: 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 agrees on filter modes and empty address lists (#13857), post-merge and genesis reward records (#13938, #13783, #13801), vmTrace steps (#13940, #13958), precheck and collision frames (#13957) and failed-frame results and labels (#13981); 2.0.0 · bec830cd still differs on all of these. trace_transaction and trace_get return null for a missing transaction (#13937), but trace_replayTransaction still errors (#14037 is open). trace_filter still matches a failed CREATE by its would-be address; raw-transaction validation, malformed-input rejection, simulation fees and block-hash filter bounds remain review areas.

reth.name: Reth
reth.summary: Reth 2.7.0 · 3d592ece, with revm-inspectors 0.44.0, ships tree-path lookup, default filter intersection, missing-replay nulls, replay transaction hashes, the genesis reward, omitted filter bounds, the omitted trace_callMany block, new-account stateDiff markers, EIP-7702 code changes and executing initcode in vmTrace, all of which differed in 2.6.0; the nightly 2.7.0 · 60aeb532, built from main after the release, returns the same responses. Remaining work includes simulation fees, the rest of vmTrace, null filter address lists (Alloy #4257, not yet in an Alloy release) and the SELFDESTRUCT payload (revm #3833).

geth.name: Geth draft fork
geth.summary: The experimental fork follows the adopted source-review stances; its checked cases agree on every assessed decision, including pending simulations, which it runs in a real pending environment; pending block traces stay blocked on the frozen chain’s empty pending block, and one H14 input policy is open; it rejects the H12 raw-transaction block argument, an extension outside the baseline. It is not upstream Geth support or a consensus vote. Filtering remains a bounded scan; pruning still needs runtime coverage.

anvil.name: Anvil
anvil.summary: Foundry’s development node, captured by replaying each chain instead of through Hive. The nightly 1.8.4 · 00989695 takes up revm-inspectors 0.44.0 (#17073), which brings the EIP-7702 stateDiff, executing-bytecode and vmTrace step fixes also in Reth 2.7.0, corrects the empty trace-type selection, omitted filter bounds and the trace_callMany default block (#17078) and returns null from trace_transaction for a missing transaction (#17089); 1.8.3 still differs on all of these. With 0.44.0 the nightly also loses the creation markers of a contract created in trace_call and reports an account created and destroyed in one transaction as deleted (open #17106 fixes both). Its own RPC layer still differs in tree-path lookup, missing blocks and replays, replay transaction hashes, conflicting data/input and zero-fee BASEFEE. Mined-trace methods also return precompile frames that its trace_call omits. The mined-probes chain cannot be replayed because Anvil cannot set a parent beacon root.

besu.observed: Individual transaction replay is unavailable.
besu.change: Add `trace_replayTransaction`; the draft requires all nine methods.

besu.observed: A recipient-only filter returns 1 of the 2 expected calls. Every recognized `mode` value is rejected with `-32602`, including `intersection` and `union`.
besu.change: Make a one-sided query select every call matching the populated list. Accept `intersection` as the default and `union` as an explicit option; reject only unknown values.

erigon.observed: Both lists are combined with OR by default (6 records instead of 1). With `mode: "intersection"`, a one-sided filter returns `[]` instead of treating the empty side as unrestricted. The unrecognized `mode: "garbage"` is accepted and treated as union.
erigon.change: Make intersection the default. Under either mode, ignore an omitted, null or empty side. Reject unknown mode values (`-32602` recommended).

reth.observed: 2.7.0 · 3d592ece and the nightly intersect both lists by default (Alloy #4216), where 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 combined them with OR (6 records instead of 1); one-sided and explicit-mode queries agree.
reth.change: No change; explicit union is retained.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd: `mode: "union"` returns the intersection (1 record instead of 6) and `mode: "garbage"` is accepted: the filter type has no `mode` field, so every request is intersected. 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 includes #13857, which adds the `mode` field, and agrees on the checked cases.
nethermind.change: Ship #13857 in a release: a validated `mode` field that accepts `intersection` (the default) and `union` and rejects other values (`-32602` recommended).

besu.observed: Treats `[]` as unrestricted. Its only H04-tagged failure, on `a/filter-from-empty-to-set`, is the SELFDESTRUCT-beneficiary record it misses under every filter (H23).
besu.change: No empty-list change; match SELFDESTRUCT by beneficiary (H23).

nethermind.observed: In 2.0.0 · bec830cd empty address lists match nothing (no records in any of the three `[]` cases), while omitted and null lists are unrestricted; 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 includes #13857 and treats `[]` as unrestricted. Nethermind is the only client that reads `[]` this way, and its own eth_getLogs treats an empty address set as any address.
nethermind.change: Ship #13857 in a release: treat `[]` as unrestricted, like an omitted or null list and like its eth_getLogs.

reth.observed: Treats `[]` as unrestricted in both builds and rejects only a null address list, because Alloy’s `TraceFilter` defaults the lists only when they are absent. Alloy #4257 fixes this and is merged, but no Alloy release carries it; 2.7.0 locks alloy-rpc-types-trace 2.5.0.
reth.change: Take up Alloy #4257 so a null list is treated as omitted.

besu.observed: PoS blocks include a synthetic PoW reward record.
besu.change: Remove the placeholder reward. This also changes which records pagination counts.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd adds a synthetic PoW reward record to PoS blocks, and `trace_block(0)` and `trace_replayBlockTransactions(0)` return -32000 because the genesis parent lookup fails. 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 includes #13938, which drops the post-merge reward, and #13783 and #13801, which return `[]` for the genesis block.
nethermind.change: Ship #13938, #13783 and #13801 in a release.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 included a block reward for the genesis coinbase in `trace_block(0)` and filters from block 0 on a PoW-genesis chain; 2.7.0 · 3d592ece and the nightly emit none (#27423).
reth.change: No change.

besu.observed: Unknown transactions can return [] and an unknown selected block returns null.
besu.change: Return `null` for an unknown transaction, so callers can distinguish absence from a transaction with no call records. Filter bounds beyond the head already return `-32602` as proposed.

erigon.observed: A missing transaction, path or replay returns null as proposed. An unknown selected block, including a block replay, returns -32000, which the rule accepts (-32001 is recommended), and a filter bound beyond the head returns [] (an explicit "waiting for spec" choice). 3.8.0-dev · a1ce80fb includes #24341 and returns -32602 for a reversed range.
erigon.change: Prefer `-32001` for an unknown selected block. Return an error for a filter bound beyond the head (`-32602` recommended) rather than `[]`, and ship the reversed-range check (#24341) in a release.

nethermind.observed: In 2.0.0 · bec830cd missing transactions or paths can produce exceptions/RPC errors, and a filter bound beyond the head returns -32000. 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 includes #13937: trace_transaction and trace_get return null for a missing transaction, while trace_replayTransaction still returns -32000 (“receipt could not be found”) and a filter bound beyond the head still returns -32000.
nethermind.change: Return `null` from trace_replayTransaction for an absent transaction too, while preserving distinct unavailable-history errors. A filter bound beyond the head already returns an error; `-32602` is recommended.

reth.observed: 2.7.0 · 3d592ece and the nightly return null for a missing individual replay (#27364) and from trace_replayBlockTransactions for an unknown block, and -32001 for a filter bound beyond the head. See the linked pruning cases for unavailable-history classification.
reth.change: Return `null` for absent transactions and an error for an unknown selected block, including a block replay (-32001 recommended), as trace_block already does (open #27478). For known transactions whose state is unavailable, return an error that reports unavailable history (`4444` recommended) rather than an internal error. A filter bound beyond the head already returns an error; `-32602` is recommended.

geth.observed: The fork follows the draft on every checked H06 case, including -32602 for a filter bound beyond the head.

anvil.observed: trace_block returns `[]` for a missing block, a missing replay returns -32001 `transaction not found`, and trace_call at a block beyond the head returns -32602. trace_replayBlockTransactions of an unknown block returns `[]`, and a filter ending one block past the head returns the head’s records instead of an error. For a missing transaction, trace_transaction returns `[]` in 1.8.3 and null in the nightly 00989695 (#17089).
anvil.change: Return `null` for a missing path or replay and an error for an unknown selected block (-32001 recommended), including the trace_call and block-replay blocks, and for a filter bound beyond the head (-32602 recommended). Ship #17089 in a release.

besu.observed: Failed frames lose result information; a failed root precompile can also lack an error.
besu.change: Keep the error on the failing frame, including a failed root precompile. Add `result: {gasUsed, output}` to REVERT frames; exceptional halts may keep omitting `result`. Use the listed labels, e.g. "Mutable Call In Static Context" and "Built-in failed". `revertReason` is outside the format and may stay as an extension once `result` is present.

nethermind.observed: In 2.0.0 · bec830cd failed frames omit their result, and failures use labels such as "Static call violation" and "Error". 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 includes #13981: a REVERT frame keeps `{gasUsed, output}`, a reverted CREATE has no address or code, and failures use the listed labels.
nethermind.change: Ship #13981 in a release.

erigon.observed: In 3.7.0 · bdc78cc4 a reverted CREATE reports `{address, code, gasUsed}` with the would-be address; exceptional halts use Go error text such as "out of gas: write protection", and a failed precheck is labelled "insufficient balance for transfer". 3.8.0-dev · a2a19253 includes #24355 and #24356: a reverted CREATE reports `{gasUsed, output}` and failures use the listed labels.
erigon.change: Ship #24355 and #24356 in a release: a reverted CREATE as `{gasUsed, output}` without address or code, and the listed failure labels.

reth.observed: A reverted CREATE reports `{address, code, gasUsed}` with the would-be address; other failures fall back to Rust `Debug` names such as `NotActivated`.
reth.change: Report a reverted CREATE as `{gasUsed, output}` without address or code, and use the listed failure labels.

geth.observed: The fork uses the draft labels, including “Out of gas” for code above the EIP-170 limit or a failed code deposit and “Invalid code” for an EIP-3541 0xEF prefix (since e26833e3), and emits no `revertReason`.

besu.observed: A successful creation reports deployed bytecode under `output`, and `creationMethod` is missing from most create frames and computed per transaction.
besu.change: Use `code` for deployed bytecode, alongside `address` and `gasUsed`. Emit `creationMethod` on every create action, from that frame’s own opcode.

besu.observed: The zero-fee call with an empty trace selection is rejected.
besu.change: Recheck after the unsigned-call fee change (H15). This case alone does not establish a separate empty-selection bug.

erigon.observed: 3.7.0 · bdc78cc4 rejects the zero-fee empty-selection call on the fee rule (H15), so no envelope can be checked. 3.8.0-dev · a1ce80fb includes #24330, runs it and returns the execution envelope.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd fails empty trace selections; 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 executes them.
nethermind.change: Execute the call and return its output with the unrequested components empty/null.

besu.observed: Marker probes execute wrong-chain and ordinary-code-sender transactions. Nonce, funds, intrinsic-gas and base-fee failures instead return empty success-shaped traces; these do not prove execution.
besu.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and reject each invalid transaction for its own violation; the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003, are recommended.

erigon.observed: 3.7.0 · bdc78cc4: marker probes execute nonce mismatches, both insufficient-funds cases and ordinary-code-sender transactions. CREATE uses the state-nonce address. Chain, intrinsic-gas and base-fee failures are rejected with -32000. 3.8.0-dev · a2a19253 includes #24329 and rejects every invalid probe, naming the violation, with -32000; the error-group codes are recommended, not required.
erigon.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and reject each invalid transaction for its own violation; the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003, are recommended.

nethermind.observed: Marker probes execute nonce mismatches and ordinary-code-sender transactions; CREATE uses the state-nonce address. Other invalid probes produce malformed JSON, which does not establish skipped validation.
nethermind.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and reject each invalid transaction for its own violation; the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003, are recommended.

reth.observed: All invalid probes in the validation corpus are rejected, using -32000 or -32003. Valid EOA/delegated controls execute, and valid execution-OOG returns a trace halt.
reth.change: Retain execution validation; the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003, are recommended.

besu.observed: Paired eth_call executes explicit zero fees with BASEFEE 0, while trace_call returns an internal error. An omitted fee is priced and charged at the base fee in trace_call but free in eth_call, and a supplied nonce that differs from the state nonce is rejected. Valid priced calls show the expected upfront debit in both methods; invalid trace fee/funding requests still produce generic internal errors.
besu.change: Match eth_call: default omitted fees to zero, zero BASEFEE for a zero effective price and ignore a supplied nonce. Retain priced accounting and return the eth_simulateV1 validation codes.

erigon.observed: 3.7.0 · bdc78cc4: eth_call uses BASEFEE 0 for explicit zero fees and debits priced gas upfront. trace_call rejects legacy zero, reprices typed zero and omitted fees to B, changes GASLIMIT and skips the sender gas debit; its stateDiff still credits tips. Both methods reject positive legacy/typed caps below B. 3.8.0-dev · a2a19253 includes #24330 and #24343: trace_call and trace_callMany price gas like eth_call, run zero and defaulted blob fees with BLOBBASEFEE 0, charge priced calls, keep the block GASLIMIT and report fee and funding rejections with the eth_simulateV1 codes (-38012 for a fee cap below the base fee). Only the refund-bound accounting checks stay unassessed, as for the Geth draft.
erigon.change: Ship #24330 and #24343 in a release: preserve the block GASLIMIT and keep the recommended eth_simulateV1 codes, keeping eth_call’s fee defaults and priced accounting.

nethermind.observed: Both tested builds use BASEFEE 0 in zero-fee eth_call but preserve B in trace_call, for explicit and omitted fees alike. Priced upfront debit matches in both methods when execution output is returned. 641592d2 fixes the release’s selection/output bugs. 2.0.0 truncates fee/funding rejections in trace_call; 2.1.0-preview · 45912ba3 includes #13666 and returns them complete but with -32000 instead of the eth_simulateV1 codes (see the [streaming investigation](../../docs/nethermind-streamed-errors.md)). An explicit zero `maxFeePerBlobGas` is rejected, and a blob fee defaulted with blob hashes present returns -32603.
nethermind.change: Zero BASEFEE whenever the effective price is zero, including omitted fees, name the violation in validation errors, with the eth_simulateV1 codes recommended; run a zero or defaulted blob fee with BLOBBASEFEE 0; retain normal priced accounting.

reth.observed: Both methods use BASEFEE 0 for explicit zero fees and both omit priced upfront gas payment: the shared call environment sets `disable_fee_charge`, added for OP operator fees (#18634, reverted in #18645, re-added in #19073), which also skips the funding check. Both accept underpriced legacy calls and reject underpriced typed caps; a tip-only request is priced at the base fee. Method consistency agrees in 200 defined-policy pairs per build; two underfunded-value families have unclassified EVM failures. Independent priced accounting/funding checks still differ.
reth.change: Keep zero-fee compatibility. Default an omitted fee cap to zero, so a zero tip-only request runs free and a positive one is rejected as tip above cap. Reject positive legacy prices below base fee, enforce funding and simulate payment/refunds/tips during execution and later calls. Agreement with eth_call is assessed separately from this accounting requirement. Whether the L1 effect of `disable_fee_charge` is intended is an open question to Reth; complying also changes its eth_call. Asked in [reth#27476](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/issues/27476) whether skipping fee charging and funding checks on L1 is intended.

geth.observed: The fork follows eth_call: a zero effective price, explicit or defaulted, runs with BASEFEE 0 and no fee effects, and priced calls are validated and charged. It is not an upstream consensus vote.

anvil.observed: An explicit zero fee keeps the block base fee visible as BASEFEE instead of 0. Priced calls settle the sender debit and coinbase tip in stateDiff, matching the proposal where the native clients do not.
anvil.change: Run a zero effective price with GASPRICE and BASEFEE 0 and no gas-fee balance effects; keep the priced settlement.

besu.observed: The `MCOPY` step omits its memory write, and CALL-family `mem` can copy the calling frame’s final RETURN. A value CALL’s `cost` includes the stipend and a precompile CALL’s the precompile cost; a CALL or CREATE that fails its precheck reports its net cost and a `sub`; a halted operation keeps a bogus `ex`.
besu.change: Include the bytes written at offset 32 in the MCOPY step’s memory delta, and stop copying the caller’s final RETURN into CALL-family `mem` (the copied bytes then conform). Exclude the stipend from value-CALL `cost`, include forwarded gas in precompile-call and failed-precheck `cost`, give a failed-precheck operation `sub: null`, and report a halted operation with `ex: null`.

erigon.observed: 3.8.0-dev · a1ce80fb reports MCOPY and MLOAD memory and the full CALL output window, and gives SELFDESTRUCT and failed-precheck calls `sub: null` (#24291). It keeps `ex` and `store` on an operation halted by an execution error, adds a synthetic STOP at the end of code and keeps undefined opcodes with cost 0.
erigon.change: Report an operation halted by an execution error with `ex: null` and no `store`, drop the synthetic STOP and omit undefined opcodes.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd: CALL steps have no `mem`, a 7400 `cost` is rewritten to 9700 (the "Parity stipend" adjustment), halted operations are deleted, a CREATE that fails its precheck reports cost 32002 without the forwarded gas, every CREATE `cost` omits the forwarded gas, DUPn pushes n words and `store` is reported only when stateDiff is also selected. 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 includes #13779, #13781, #13782, #13940 and #13958 and agrees on the checked cases.
nethermind.change: Ship the vmTrace fixes of 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 in a release.

geth.observed: The fork follows the step rules on every checked case; a static-context SSTORE that halts reports cost 0, which the implementation-defined halted-operation cost allows.

reth.observed: Reth 2.7.0 · 3d592ece and the nightly lock revm-inspectors 0.44.0, which fixes the pre-operation `used` and missing `store` of 2.6.0’s 0.43.0 and reports the bytes a CALL copied, which the rule accepts, but reports no MLOAD memory, adds a synthetic STOP, gives precompile and empty-code callees a null `sub` and a failed-precheck call a `sub`, and keeps undefined opcodes.
reth.change: Report MLOAD memory (#504 left it out), drop the synthetic STOP, give precompile and empty-code callees `{code: "0x", ops: []}` and a failed-precheck call `sub: null`, and omit undefined opcodes.

anvil.observed: 1.8.3 locks revm-inspectors 0.43.0 (whole-memory `mem`, pre-operation `used`, no `store`). The nightly 00989695 takes up 0.44.0 and agrees with Reth 2.7.0: no MLOAD memory, a synthetic STOP after the last instruction, and a `sub` on a call that fails its precheck.
anvil.change: The revm-inspectors changes listed for Reth; 1.8.3 also needs the 0.44.0 bump (#17073) in a release.

besu.observed: The identity precompile returns bytes in the execution envelope but not its call frame.
besu.change: Copy the precompile’s return bytes into the call-frame result as well.

besu.observed: CREATE and SELFDESTRUCT address queries disagree with the corresponding block trace.
besu.change: Match creation by creator/created address, SELFDESTRUCT by executing account/beneficiary, and rewards by `author` on the recipient side.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd never matches rewards by `toAddress`; 2.1.0-preview · 45912ba3 includes #13800 and matches all eight rewards by author. Both builds match a failed CREATE as a recipient of its attempted address through the internal `action.To`. 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 includes #13981, so the reverted CREATE record no longer shows that address, but `TxTraceFilter` still matches it. Alloy (Reth) and Erigon 3.7.0 show the same policy difference through the failed result address.
nethermind.change: Ship reward matching by `author` (#13800). Match a failed CREATE only on the addresses its record reports, so it has no recipient match (the H23 adoption shared with Erigon and Alloy), while keeping sender-only matching and empty recipient filters unchanged. #13981 removed the address from the record but not from the filter.

erigon.observed: In 3.7.0 · bdc78cc4 a failed CREATE matches its attempted address through the failed result address, the same policy difference Nethermind (`action.To`) and Alloy (Reth) show; 3.8.0-dev · a2a19253 reports no address for it (#24355) and returns no match. From source, rewards are emitted for a coinbase in `toAddress` only in blocks the address indexes select: to-only and union filters return them, while intersection mode intersects the from and to txNum bitmaps, so `rewards-intersection` returns `[]` on both builds.
erigon.change: Ship #24355 in a release, giving a failed CREATE no recipient match, the H23 adoption shared with Nethermind and Alloy, while keeping sender-only matching and empty recipient filters unchanged.

reth.observed: A failed CREATE matches its attempted address through Alloy’s failed result address, the same policy difference Erigon and Nethermind show. A post-Cancun SELFDESTRUCT to self has no executing account or beneficiary, so address filters miss it: revm skips the inspector callback (revm #3834).
reth.change: Give a failed CREATE no recipient match, the H23 adoption shared with Erigon and Nethermind. The SELFDESTRUCT payload follows from revm #3833 once it reaches revm-inspectors and Reth.

besu.observed: A handled child failure can mark a successful parent or sibling as failed.
besu.change: Track errors per frame; a caught failure must not change the outcome of another frame.

besu.observed: A range filter differs from concatenating the same blocks’ traces across a fork boundary.
besu.change: Trace each block from its parent’s post-block state with its own pre-block system calls, under its own fork rules, so range filtering agrees with per-block tracing. Swapping the protocol spec alone leaves rewards, withdrawals and system calls between blocks unapplied.

besu.observed: Nested precompile frames are omitted even when their value is nonzero. A CALL that fails its balance precheck has no frame, and a CREATE that fails it leaves a successful-looking frame at `[0]`, moves the real creation below it and reports the root as using no gas.
besu.change: Retain nested precompile frames with transferred or inherited nonzero value (#11360). Continue omitting zero-value nested frames and retaining root frames. Give a CALL or CREATE that fails its balance or depth precheck a failed frame with error "Insufficient balance for transfer", no result and no children, as Besu's callTracer already records it; no submitted fix covers this.

nethermind.observed: In 2.0.0 · bec830cd a CALL or CREATE that fails its balance precheck has no frame, and a CREATE2 address collision has no frame either; its callTracer also omits the precheck failure. 2.2.0-preview · 287f54f0 includes #13957 and emits the failed frames, labelled "Insufficient balance for transfer" and "Contract address collision", in trace_* and in its callTracer.
nethermind.change: Ship #13957 in a release.

geth.observed: The fork emits a failed frame with its action and error label, no result and no subtraces for a CALL or CREATE that fails its precheck, as the revised rule requires.

anvil.observed: trace_transaction, trace_block and trace_filter return the calltree’s nested zero-value identity call as a frame, shifting its siblings; trace_call and the replays omit it. Mined traces are built from the frames recorded at mining time without the active precompile set.
anvil.change: Build mined traces with the same precompile filter as simulations: omit nested zero-value precompile frames and number the emitted tree.

erigon.observed: Root and nested `trace_get` requests fail or select the wrong record.
erigon.change: Interpret the selector as one `traceAddress` path: `[]` selects the root, `[0]` its first child.

nethermind.observed: `trace_get` returns a list and treats positions differently from a nested path; `[]` returns `[]`.
nethermind.change: Return one object for one `traceAddress` path. `[]` selects the root; a missing path returns `null`. This changes the response type.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 used a flat selector; 2.7.0 · 3d592ece and the nightly select the requested tree path (#27366) and match these cases.
reth.change: No change; existing flat-index callers need a migration path.

anvil.observed: `trace_get` indexes the flattened frame list and needs exactly one index: `[]` and nested paths return null, and `[1]` returns the second frame in list order.
anvil.change: Interpret the selector as one `traceAddress` path: `[]` selects the root, `[0]` its first child.

erigon.observed: No envelope deviation; output differs only through the H15 GASLIMIT environment.
erigon.change: None for the envelope; its trace_call reports GASLIMIT 2^256−1, an H15 environment difference.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd loses nonempty execution output with stateDiff-only selections; 2.1.0-preview · 45912ba3 retains it.
nethermind.change: Always retain output bytes. The return-42 fixture should still return its 32-byte word when only state differences are requested.

anvil.observed: 1.8.3 treats an empty trace-type list in trace_call as `["trace"]`, so it returns call frames that were not requested. The nightly 00989695 includes #17078 and returns `trace: []` with the execution output.

erigon.observed: Malformed raw transactions and an unknown option use error codes other than `-32602`, and an unknown filter field is accepted. 3.7.0 drops `input` and every post-Berlin call field, so an `input`-only call runs with empty calldata. 3.8.0-dev · a2a19253 includes #24290, #24294, #24334, #24351 and #24336: it decodes `input` and the post-Berlin fields, treats an explicit null as omitted, rejects a chainId for another chain and rejects disagreeing `data` and `input` with -32602.
erigon.change: Reject malformed input, unknown filter fields and unknown trace types (`-32602` recommended), separately from execution rejection. Ship the call-field fixes in a release.

nethermind.observed: Malformed raw input, negative filter count and integer paths expose validation differences across the captured builds. An unpriced call with a null `blobVersionedHashes` or `authorizationList` takes that member’s transaction type: 2.1.0-preview · 45912ba3 rejects it with -32000 (“need at least 1 blob”, “EIP-7702 transaction cannot be used to create contract”) and 2.0.0 truncates the authorizationList response.
nethermind.change: Reject malformed input, such as a negative filter count or disagreeing `data` and `input` (`-32602` recommended). Treat a null member as omitted, so it selects no transaction type.

besu.observed: Wrong address-list types and negative count can return results rather than invalid params.
